title: Clausulae Timendi
subtitle: Timeo ne venias — 'I fear THAT you will come', ne inverso.
objectives: Formare clausulas post verba timendi (timeo, vereor, metuo)
Applicare regulam inversam: ne = 'that' (timor positivus), ut = 'that...not' (timor negativus)
Distinguere hanc constructionem a clausulis finalibus, ubi ne/ut habent significationem normalem
Applicare consecutionem temporum in clausulis timendi

content.intro: 'Timeo ne iterum discedas,' dicit Iulia Lucio. Non significat 'I fear that you WON'T leave' — significat EXACTE OPPOSITUM: 'I fear that you WILL leave'. Haec inversio semantica est trap frequentissima Gradus V.
content.explanation:
“Timeō nē iterum discēdās,” dīcit Iūlia Lūciō. “Vereor ut satis temporis hīc maneās.”

Notāvistīne: 'nē discēdās' nōn significat 'that you won't leave' — significat EXACTĒ OPPOSITUM: 'that you WILL leave' (timor positīvus, rem malam ēventūram). Et 'ut maneās' significat 'that you will NOT stay' (timor negātīvus). Post verba timendī (timeō, vereor, metuō), particulae nē et ut INVERTUNT significātiōnem ūsuālem.

rules.heading: a) Ne = 'That' (Timor de Re Quae Eveniat)
rules.body: Timeō nē veniat. ('I fear THAT he WILL come' — timeō rem positīvam ēventūram.) Litterāliter: 'I fear LEST he come', sed Anglicē nātūrālius 'that he will come'.

rules.heading: b) Ut = 'That...Not' (Timor de Re Quae Non Eveniat)
rules.body: Timeō ut veniat. ('I fear THAT he will NOT come' — timeō āctiōnem positīvam NŌN ēventūram.) Alternātīva magis clāra (et frequentior in ūsū posteriōre): nē nōn: Timeō nē nōn veniat. (eadem significātiō, minus ambigua.)

rules.heading: c) Cur Haec Inversio?
rules.body: Historicē, 'nē' hīc retinet suum sēnsum orīginālem prohibitīvum ('let it not happen that...') — timor ipse est DĒ EVENTŪ malō (ex perspectīvā timentis), quī grammaticē est 'nē' (id nē fīat). Logica inversa, sed cōnsistēns sī sīc intellegitur.

rules.heading: d) Consecutio Temporum
rules.body: Regula normalis applicātur: coniūnctīvus praesēns/perfectus post prīmārium; imperfectus/plūsquamperfectus post historicum.

examples: Timeo ne hostes veniant. — I fear that the enemies will come.
Vereor ut satis pecuniae habeamus. — I fear that we do not have enough money.
Timuit ne urbs caperetur. — He feared that the city would be captured.
Metuo ne nimis tardus sim. — I fear that I am too late.
Timebamus ne pater noster moreretur. — We feared that our father would die.

commonMistakes.wrong: 'Timeō nē veniās' vertitur 'I fear that you won't come', per applicationem regulae normalis 'nē' = 'that...not'.
commonMistakes.right: Post verba timendi, 'nē' significat 'that' (timor positivus): 'I fear that you WILL come'.
commonMistakes.why: Haec est unica constructio ubi ne/ut invertunt significationem normalem — memoranda separatim ab omnibus aliis clausulis coniunctivi.

commonMistakes.wrong: 'Ut' post verbum timendi tractatur ut habens significationem normalem finalis ('in order that').
commonMistakes.right: Post verba timendi, 'ut' significat 'that...not' (timor negativus) — inversum quoque.
commonMistakes.why: Ambae particulae (ne/ut) sunt invertit hic, non solum una.

exercises.title: Timeo Ne Discedas
exercises.passage: “Timeō nē iterum discēdās,” dīcit Iūlia Lūciō. “Vereor ut satis temporis hīc maneās — dux enim tē saepe vocat.” Lūcius eam cōnsōlātur: “Nē timeās, Iūlia. Metuō quidem nē tibi trīstitiam faciam discēdendō, sed semper redībō.”

items.explanation: 'Timeo ne iterum discedas' — timet EVENTUM discessus.

options: ita — 'vereor ut maneas' significat timere quod NON manebit satis diu
items.explanation: 'Vereor ut maneas' = 'I fear that you will NOT stay [long enough]'.

options: I fear that you will not come
I fear that you will come
I do not fear your coming
I fear that we have enough money
I fear that we do NOT have enough money

items.prompt: Alternativa magis clara pro 'ut' (timor negativus) est:
items.explanation: nē nōn: eadem significatio, minus ambigua.
Timor positivus, historicum: nē + coniunctivus imperfectus.

summary: Post verba timendi (timeō, vereor, metuō): nē = 'that' (timor positivus); ut = 'that...not' (timor negativus).
Haec inversio est unica in tota syntaxi coniunctivi Latini.
